title: Ops standdown & rapid redeploy — internal announce + Q&A crib
body:
PURPOSE
Short scratch: prep a quick internal announcement, speaker notes, and Q&A crib for the team-facing comms when we initiate a temporary ops standdown + rapid redeploy window. This is a working draft — fill in specifics from postmortem and SRE timeline before send.

SITUATION SUMMARY (to surface at top of comm)
- What happened (one-liner): Regressing memory allocator bug caused intermittent host OOMs in US-west serving pool during 2026-02-18 03:00–04:10 UTC, leading to degraded latency and a small percentage of failed requests.
- Immediate impact: ~2.4% of requests returned 5xx or timed out, median tail latency spiked for ~40 minutes. No customer data exposure.
- Why we need a standdown + redeploy: rolling redeploy with the fixed allocator + kernel patch will restore headroom and remove risk of recurrence while we rewarm caches and validate KV integrity. We want to be explicit about scope and duration to reduce surprise.

TIMING & SCOPE (rough)
- Proposed window: start 2026-02-21 01:00 UTC, target end 2026-02-21 03:00 UTC (2-hour slot).
- Affected surfaces: Hosted API (US-west region) for text gen & embeddings. Dedicated/private customers not on the affected pool unaffected unless they explicitly use the US-west shard.
- User-visible behavior: brief elevated latency during warm-up (1–5 mins per node) and small % of request throttling during the first 30 minutes as we ramp.

COMMUNICATION OBJECTIVES
1) Reassure: we understand impact, we fixed root cause in code, we control rollout (can pause/rollback).
2) Be concrete: what customers will see and for how long.
3) Ask for help: operations support (oncall overlap), and devs available for immediate rollback.
4) Reduce noise: provide one canonical Slack thread and status page update.

PLANNED ANNOUNCEMENT (Slack + All-hands snippet)
- Short Slack message (ops-alerts channel):
  "Heads-up: we will run a planned 2-hr rolling redeploy in US-west on 2026-02-21 01:00–03:00 UTC to push allocator+kernel fixes for recent OOM regressions. Expect transient latency as nodes warm; no customer data impacted. Oncall: @kai, SRE lead: @sahana. Status updates will be in #infra-status and on the status page. Ping this thread if you see something unexpected."

- All-hands 60s slide speak notes:
  "We discovered a memory allocator regression that caused some OOMs in a subset of US-west inference hosts. We've built a fix, validated it in canaries, and plan a controlled rolling redeploy early Saturday to fully mitigate risk. Expected impact is limited to transient latency while caches rehydrate; dedicated tenants not using the pool are unaffected. Ops will monitor and can pause if needed. We'll follow with a brief postmortem and timeline."

SPEAKER NOTES (ops lead)
- Opening: one-line recap + why we chose redeploy vs other mitigation.
- Assurance: canary results (X canary nodes for Y minutes, error rate back to baseline).
- Contingency: rollback plan (how to detect, who authorizes rollback, ~5–10 minute RTO), traffic isolation knobs, and fallback to smaller-model pool if latency persists.
- Ask: coverage for the window from infra, runtime, and console teams (list of people already cc'd).

Q&A CRIB (for slido/all-hands and Slack thread)
Q: Will dedicated/private customers be affected?
A: Only if they route through the affected US-west hosts; customers with pinned capacity in other regions are not impacted. We will post explicit list of affected customers on the internal status doc if needed.

Q: Why not perform the patch during regular maintenance window?
A: The fix needs a rolling restart to clear kernel-level allocator state; delaying risks recurrence and customer impact. We chose the slot with lowest expected user traffic.

Q: Risk of data loss?
A: No evidence of data exposure or loss. We validated request logs and KV integrity during canaries.

Q: How do we detect if rollback is needed?
A: Predefined SLO thresholds (error rate > 1.5% or 99.9th latency > 3x baseline for >10 min). If thresholds hit, SRE lead raises rollback; engineering will revert to previous tagged deploy (instructions in playbook).

ACTION CHECKLIST (quick)
- Pre-deploy (T-24h): update status page draft, notify CS (customer success) for any VIP customers, prepare rollback artifact (image tag + runbook). Owner: Kai.
- Canary (T-2h): run on 5 canary nodes for 30m, monitor errors & KV checks. Owner: Rowan.
- Deploy (T): staggered rolling restart with health gates every 5 nodes. Owner: SRE team.
- Post (T+1h): run smoke tests, verify latency and error rate stable for 30m, update status page. Owner: Harper.

NOTES & SCRIPTS (tickets/snippets to paste)
- Rollback command: kubectl -n inference set image deployment/runtime runtime=ghcr.io/redwood/runtime:release-2026-02-14
- Health-check query: curl -sSf -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" https://us-west.api.redwood.ai/v1/health | jq .
- Postmortem stub: confluence link (TBD) — attach perf graphs, kernel traces, allocator diff.

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs in this draft
- Confirm exact canary node count and hostnames (Rowan)
- Finalize exact start time after sync with Console team DNS TTL windows (Kai)
- Decide whether to send outbound customer email for top-10 customers (CS lead to decide)

TONE GUIDANCE (for sender)
- Keep it utilitarian and short; avoid technical deep-dive in the first announcement. Use the all-hands slot for context + expectation setting.
- If customers ask technical follow-ups, link to the postmortem rather than embedding long logs in Slack.

SAMPLE CUSTOMER-FACING BLURB (if CS needs it)
Subject: Planned maintenance — rolling redeploy in US-west (brief impact)
Body (short): "We are performing a planned rolling update to improve stability in our US-west inference pool on 2026-02-21 01:00–03:00 UTC. You may see transient increases in latency for a short period while we validate the update; no customer data will be affected. We will notify you when the work is complete."

END NOTES
- This is intentionally a lightweight crib — populate exact metrics and names before posting.
- After redeploy, schedule a 30-minute sync to confirm postmortem timeline and communication cadence.

Quick edit log:
- 2025-11-04: initial sketch (Harper)
- 2026-02-18: update with incident summary (Harper)
- 2026-02-20: add final canary plan + rollback commands (Rowan, Kai)
